chunks: That was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from some of his companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them):

Regarding the woman who marries during her waiting period, he said: 'They are separated, and she observes one waiting period for both [marriages]. If she gives birth to a child after six months or more, the child belongs to the second husband; and if she gives birth to a child in less than six months, the child belongs to the first husband.'

And whenever the woman marries during her waiting period out of ignorance, then her husband accuses her of adultery for what she did, the penalty of the accuser (hadd al-qadhf) becomes obligatory upon him. And if she was knowledgeable about it, nothing becomes obligatory upon him, and the penalty becomes obligatory upon her, which is the penalty of the adulterer.

key_terms.حَدُّ الْقَاذِفِ: The penalty of the accuser (hadd al-qadhf)
key_terms.سِتَّةِ أَشْهُرٍ: Six months, the legal threshold for determining paternity in case of dual marriage
key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period (iddah) observed by a woman after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.يُفَرَّقُ بَيْنَهُمَا: They are separated (the marriage is annulled)

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal rulings for a woman who marries during her waiting period (iddah)?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from the Imams (likely Imam al-Sadiq) regarding the validity of a second marriage contracted during the *iddah* of the first. The text establishes a clear jurisprudential distinction: if the first husband falsely accuses her of adultery due to her remarriage, he is liable for *qadhf* if she was ignorant of the ruling, but exempt if she was knowledgeable, in which case she bears the penalty for adultery. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the woman's legal awareness (*'ilm*) in determining the reciprocal rights and penalties between spouses.
